links.outcome: LLM accuracy on oncology questions versus human exam benchmark
links.effect: Only GPT-4 performed above the 50th percentile of the human benchmark; performance was worse in clinical oncology subcategories than in foundational topics; all LLMs had clinically significant error rates.
links.quote: Relative to a human benchmark (2013 and 2014 examination results), GPT-4 was the only model to perform above the 50th percentile.

links.outcome: Accuracy of question subsets selected by prompt repetition consistency and self-appraised confidence
links.effect: Combining model selection, prompt repetition, and confidence self-appraisal identified high-performing question subgroups with accuracies of 81.7% (Claude-v1) and 81.1% (GPT-4).
links.quote: A combination of model selection, prompt repetition, and confidence self-appraisal allowed for the identification of high-performing subgroups of questions with observed accuracies of 81.7 and 81.1% in the Claude-v1 and GPT-4 models, respectively.

links.outcome: Overconfidence in LLM self-appraised confidence scores
links.effect: Study reports examples of overconfidence and consistent inaccuracies across all LLMs, despite confidence self-appraisal being useful for identifying higher-accuracy subgroups.
links.quote: Although this performance is impressive, all LLMs continue to have clinically significant error rates, including examples of overconfidence and consistent inaccuracies.

links.outcome: Model accuracy differences across malignancy types by patient sex predominance
links.effect: Worse performance observed within clinical oncology for female-predominant malignancies.
links.quote: Within the clinical oncology subdomain, worse performance was observed in female-predominant malignancies.

unlisted_practices: Comparing multiple LLMs head-to-head on a standardized question battery
Using a novel validation question set to avoid training-data contamination

screen.practice: prompt repetition and confidence self-appraisal to flag reliable outputs
screen.reason: The study benchmarks several LLMs on clinical oncology questions and explicitly tests strategies (prompt repetition consistency and self-appraised confidence score filtering) as a deployment guardrail to identify reliable model outputs.

primary.practice: prompt repetition and confidence self-appraisal filtering
